name: LF351 / LF353 / LF347 (single/dual/quad BiFET, JFET-input)
tagline: National's 1977 BI-FET II JFET dual: a cheap TL072-class op-amp found in vintage audio and synth gear, valued mostly for period-correct restorations.
technology: BiFET: matched high-voltage JFET input pair plus bipolar output stage on one monolithic chip, with an internally trimmed input offset. National called it 'BI-FET II' (the TI LF353-N datasheet SNOSBH3F keeps that wording). Internally compensated, 0-70 °C commercial grade. National's application hints say each amplifier is biased by its own zener reference (DS005649).
manufacturers: National Semiconductor (originator; BI-FET II LF351/LF353/LF347 advertised in Electronic Design, 27 Sep 1977; acquired by TI 2011)
Texas Instruments (two lineages: its own LF353 SLOS012 / LF347 SLOS013 from March 1987, and the ex-National LF353-N SNOSBH3, LF147/LF347-N SNOSBH1 and LF351-N)
Motorola / ON Semiconductor ('Family of BIFET Operational Amplifiers' LF347/LF351/LF353; ON discontinuance notice 10109 around 1999-2000 covers LF353 variants)
Fairchild Semiconductor (LF351, Rev 1.0.1, PDF created June 2001)

reputation.summary: NOT WEB-VERIFIED: this pass spent no searches on listening or measurement reports. The discovery notes describe the LF353 as a vintage BiFET dual in 1980s-90s consumer and synth gear, called smooth or warm by some listeners and ordinary by measurement-minded reviewers. On paper it is a TL072-class part: 16-18 nV/rtHz and 3-4 MHz. TI lists 'Pro Audio Mixers' among its applications, and National specified THD <0.02%. Its appeal is originality in restorations, not performance.
typical_uses: pro audio mixers (TI SLOS012C application list)
preamp, tone-control and filter stages in vintage gear (discovery notes, unverified)
synthesizer and modular CV/VCO/VCF circuits (e.g. open4Umodular subosc BOM 'LF353 or TL072')
active filters, integrators, sample-and-hold, D/A converters (TI and National datasheets)
budget Chinese DACs (a Xiang Sheng DAC-01A review lists OPA2604 x1 and LF353N x2; low confidence)
caveats: Noisier than bipolar audio duals: 16-18 nV/rtHz against about 5 nV/rtHz for an NE5532. It matters with low-impedance sources.
Offset up to 10 mV (13 mV over temperature), so DC-coupled stages need trimming, a servo or a coupling capacitor.
National documents phase reversal: taking either input below the negative common-mode limit forces the output high (no latch). Keep inputs at least 3-4 V above V-. TI SLOS012C does not mention it.
TI recommends +/-3.5 V minimum, while National says zener biasing gives normal operation from +/-6 V. Commercial 0-70 °C only.
Output specified only into 2 k/10 k loads, so not for 600-ohm or headphone loads.

Specs differ by vendor and by TI lineage (TI LF353 3 MHz/18 nV; LF353-N and National 4 MHz/16 nV; ST 4 MHz/15 nV, 16 V/us). An 'LF353' from another maker, or LF353P against LF353M/NOPB, is not the same datasheet.
Never let an input go below the negative supply: National warns this can destroy the unit.

silicon_changes.vendor: Texas Instruments (TI's own LF353, SLOS012 lineage; not the ex-National LF353-N)
silicon_changes.when: PCN 20220615003.1, dated 16 Jun 2022 (samples until 16 Jul 2022; proposed first ship 16 Sep 2022). PCN 20230627002.1 is numbered June 2023; one search summary gives its PCN date as 25 Oct 2023 (unverified). TI E2E threads 1442987 and 1512001 (2024-2025) discuss post-PCN parts.
part_numbers_affected: LF353P / LF353PE4 (likely; not itemised in any retrieved source)
silicon_changes.identification: The part number and marking are unchanged, and no SLOS012 revision newer than C (Mar 2016) was found. Per search summaries, PCN 20220615003.1 moves the fab from SH-BIP-1 (Sherman, TX) to RFAB (Richardson, TX), changes die rev C to A and adds MLA (Kuala Lumpur) assembly. PCN 20230627002.1 shows the die-revision field going from C/E/F/H to A. The only external clue is the date code or lot relative to the first-ship dates (from about Sep 2022); TI lot/fab trace data is definitive. The National-design LF353-N (LF353N/NOPB, LF353M/NOPB, LF353MX/NOPB) is a separate product and is not covered by these PCNs.
silicon_changes.summary: TI moved its own LF353 from Sherman to RFAB on a new die. On E2E (1512001), TI says PCNs 20220615003.1 and 20230627002.1 'introduced an entirely new die' with an entirely new design, and the guaranteed datasheet limits did not change. In E2E 1442987 ('LF353: new part parameter change'), TI says the new part's bandwidth rose to about 4.5 MHz because of the fab change and warns of possible stability issues in existing circuits. The same PCN's new die for the TL082 adds clamp diodes to VCC+ (E2E 1428797); that the LF353 die has them too is likely but not confirmed. No typical-value changes were found for noise, slew, bias or supply current.

spec_deltas.parameter: Die revision (PCN fields, per search summaries)

spec_deltas.after: about 4.5 MHz (TI E2E statement; not a datasheet value)

spec_deltas.before: no clamp to V+ reported (legacy die)
spec_deltas.after: clamp diodes to VCC+ reported for the same PCN's TL082 new die; unconfirmed for LF353

spec_deltas.parameter: Slew rate / input bias / supply current (typ)

silicon_changes.audio_impact: About 50% more real bandwidth under unchanged limits points to different compensation and input stage. This changes phase margin and HF behaviour in active filters, tone stacks, unity-gain followers and buffers driving cable or capacitive loads. Users report stability problems in existing designs; the E2E thread suggests about 10 pF across a 30 kohm feedback resistor as a fix in one case. A new-die LF353 in a vintage design can sound different or oscillate even though the paper specs are the same. Noise and THD differences were not quantified.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: medium: pin-compatible with unchanged guaranteed limits, but TI confirms an entirely new die with about 50% more bandwidth, and users report stability and behaviour differences in existing circuits.
silicon_changes.verification: Four searches. PCN 20220615003.1's title, 16 Jun 2022 date, 16 Sep 2022 first ship and LF353 coverage are confirmed. E2E 1512001 ('entirely new die', limits unchanged) is confirmed. E2E 1442987 (about 4.5 MHz BW from the fab change, possible stability issues) is confirmed. PCN 20230627002.1 covers LF353DR with 'die changed as a result of the process change' (a search hit on the Farnell PDF). No SLOS012 revision newer than C was found.

Search summaries also loosely associated LF347 with PCNs 20220615003.1 and 20230627002.1 (the LF353 new-die PCNs); both are unconfirmed.

National lineage: orderables LF353N, LF353M and LF353MX (/NOPB under TI), datasheet National DS005649 or TI SNOSBH3 (lf353-n.pdf, ti.com/product/LF353-N), 4 MHz. RS Online lists LF353P at 3 MHz and LF353M/NOPB, LF353MX/NOPB and LF353N/NOPB at 4 MHz. Pre-2011 National parts carry the NS logo. Top-mark details are unverified.
silicon_changes.summary: TI sells two products under near-identical numbers. National's LF353 (TI LF353-N) is rated 4 MHz and 16 nV/rtHz (RS = 100 ohm), with THD <0.02%. TI's own LF353 is rated 3 MHz and 18 nV/rtHz with no THD figure, the same numbers as its TL07x. DC specs (VOS, IB, ICC, SR 13 V/us) match. Since the 2022-2023 PCNs, TI's own LF353 is itself a new RFAB die (see the die-redesign entry), so the gap between the two lineages may have changed. That TI's 1987 part is its own die is likely but inferred.

counterfeit_notes: No LF353-specific counterfeit reports were checked in this pass. It is a very cheap commodity part, so remarking pays little, but recycled or remarked DIP pulls from marketplace sellers are common for all classic op-amps. Buy TI or ST stock from authorised distributors. Motorola/ON LF35x parts were discontinued around 1999-2000 (ON notice 10109), so 'new' ON-marked stock is old or suspect. Current TI parts are marked LF353P (PDIP) or LF353 (SOIC) per TI's addendum. 'LF353AN/BN' or TO-99 'LF353H' parts are genuine National grades from before 2000; offers of them as new production are suspect. When TI stopped using the NS logo on ex-National (-N, /NOPB) parts was not verified.
alternatives: TL072 / TL072H (TI; TL072H is TI's redesigned TL07x)
OPA1642 (TI JFET-input audio dual, low noise)
NE5532 / LM4562 (bipolar, much lower voltage noise for low-impedance sources)

revision_chain_notes:
TI SLOS012 (LF353): March 1987 original (D2997), then revised May 1988 (in the 1989 data book; Rev A mapping inferred), then Rev B August 1994, then Rev C March 2016 (still current). Missing: a copy whose header says 'SLOS012A', and a copy with an explicit 'SLOS012B' header (the Cornell copies are probable). This round found new copies (Octopart 115479 and a clvaw-cdnwnd hobby copy, both with the old-style title, probably Rev B or earlier; Mouser 443390 in new format, probably Rev C; LCSC C7918; Octopart 7272549 and 7283884), but none shows its revision letter.

TI SLOS013 (LF347): March 1987 original, then Rev A (missing), then Rev B August 1994, then Rev C March 2016 (content not seen). Nothing new this round.

TI SLOS014 (LF351), new this round: March 1987 original (1989 data book), then Rev A (missing), then Rev B March 1987 - revised August 1994 (docs.rs-online.com copy, header seen). Also found: Farnell 83758 copy with the shorter 'LF351 JFET-INPUT OPERATIONAL AMPLIFIER' title (revision not shown, possibly a different edition), plus alldatasheet 462261 and chipfind. Missing: any post-1994 revision and the current TI LF351 status.

National DS005649 (LF353): 1977 Electronic Design ad, then the 1980 Linear Databook, then 1980s-1990s databook editions (missing), then about April 1998 (inferred from SNOSBH3F), then August 2000, then TI SNOSBH3 Rev A-E (all missing), then Rev F March 2013. New copies (UCSB lab copy, alldatasheet 95565, Octopart 8188024, datasheetspdf 64812) do not show their edition. National DS005647 (LF147/LF347): May 1999 (inferred), then August 2000, then SNOSBH1 A-C (missing), then D March 2013. The National LF351 new-format doc number was not found, and neither was the SNOS number for LF351-N.

ST Doc ID 2153 (LF253/LF353): an older SGS-Thomson/ST 'LF153 LF253 - LF353' edition (undated; the digchip 456 and alldatasheet 22737 copies probably hold it), then Rev 1 and Rev 2 (missing), then Rev 3 March 2010 (now also confirmed at st.com lf253.pdf). ST LF247/LF347: current URL st.com lf247.pdf (title 'lf247 lf347 - wide bandwidth quad j-fet operational amplifiers', Doc ID and revision not shown), and an older edition that includes LF147 (alldatasheet 22732); Doc ID and revision chain missing. ST LF351: current st.com lf351.pdf is new-format ('Wide bandwidth single JFET operational amplifiers'), with an older edition probably at alldatasheet 22735; Doc ID and revisions missing.

Motorola/ON (LF347/LF351/LF353 family sheet, 4 pages): Motorola edition copies found (alldatasheet 11661/11657/11651, futurlec LF351N.pdf, datasheetq), and a combined 'LF347, B LF351 LF353 JFET Input Operational Amplifiers' sheet (yumpu; probably ON). The Motorola '/D' doc number, 'Rev n' and dates were not shown. The ON discontinuance was about 1999-2000 (PCN 10109/10127).

Fairchild LF351: Rev 1.0.1 (2001) is the only revision known. A Mouser 2/308 copy was found (revision not shown).

No new legacy vendor URLs (national.com / focus.ti.com / st.com archive) turned up in the search results. The archive seeds listed are the two legacy URLs already in the known list.
